newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lower coconut oil output seen boosting prices.
newsitem.headline: Lower coconut oil output seen boosting prices.

text.p: Expectations of lower Philippine coconut oil output had brought stocks drawdowns in the U.S., Europe and other importing countries and this should boost prices, the independent newsletter Oil World said on Tuesday.
Rising Indonesian exports would not be sufficient to offset lower production in the Philippines.
During July/September 1996, copra output in the Philippines probably declined by more than a third.
As a result, coconut oil exports were at 175,000 tonnes and coconut meal at 96,000 tonnes in that period, compared with 302,000 and 221,000 tonnes respectively in the same period last year.
Rotterdam coconut prices rose to $730 for Nov/Dec shipment on Oct 31 from $717 a week earlier and versus $720 in mid-September.
Coconut oil for Oct/Nov traded at $745 cif in Europe on Monday.
U.S. coconut oil stocks were at 38,000 tonnes at the end of September compared with 74,000 tonnes a year earlier. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
